newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin signs string of decrees on military reform.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin signs string of decrees on military reform.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin signed on Wednesday a string of decrees to reorganise and reform the armed forces, Russian news agencies said.

Details of the decrees were not immediately available, but the agencies quoted Yeltsin as saying the reorganisation covered the land forces, missile units and air defence forces. Yeltsin also confirmed his earlier plan to trim the armed forces to 1.2 milllion by cutting half a million servicemen.

Yeltsin made the announcement to Russian reporters after meeting Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin at the government residence in the northwestern region of Karelia, where the Kremlin leader is on holiday.
"The president told journalists there would be an end to excessive diversification of the armed forces," Itar-Tass news agency said.
This would involve combining all the branches of the missile forces and scrapping the command of the ground forces, whose functions would be taken over by military districts.

Yeltsin said the defence ministry apparatus would not be allowed to eat up more than one percent of the military budget. "In other words...this would mean cutting the apparatus in half," Tass quoted Yeltsin as saying.
